title: Graph-Based Personalized Memory for LLM Agents: Representation, Evolution, Retrieval, and Evaluation
mechanism: Add an explicit typed-relation user/preference subgraph layer on top of chitta's existing triplet store: represent user attributes/preferences/constraints as first-class nodes with typed edges (has_preference, contradicts, supersedes) and evidence links back to source episodes, then retrieve via graph traversal instead of RRF over flat memory lanes for personalization-shaped queries

expected_gain.rationale: chitta already has triplets, graph_pagerank, graph_traverse, and contradiction detection (detect_contradictions/resolve_contradiction) per inventory §5-6; gap is a personalization-specific typed schema (preference/constraint edge types) and a retrieval path that routes to graph traversal instead of the current hybrid RRF default, not the underlying graph primitives

cost.blast_radius: chitta-mcp/server.py recall gateway (new strategy=graph_personal option), chitta/src/handlers/field_memory_recall.cpp triplet schema, no daemon storage-format change expected

evidence.claim: Survey frames graph-based memory as explicit typed relations + temporal context + evidence links, organized around representation/evolution/retrieval/evaluation lifecycle stages
Paper says fragmentation exists between personalized-agent memory work and generic graph memory frameworks
